purpose: Four dated pre-draft first-round boards for the 2006 NBA Draft (researched, October 2026). Draft-night evidence for every club's board; never the real draft result. Each board is a published mock draft: rank_by_player is the slot the mock gave the player.
status: researched; every board's publication date sourced and before the draft's first selection (June 28, 2006, evening). Names normalized to Basketball-Reference spellings; the source spelling is noted where it differs.
first_round_only: runtime/draft.py imputes slot 31 for a player absent from a board here, so only first-round boards are kept in this file. The two-round mocks and Chad Ford's top-45 board are research mocks in nba_2006_prospect_evidence.json (research_mocks), each with its own rank for an unlisted player.
same_sources_in_prospect_evidence: nba_2006_prospect_evidence.json carries these four boards' slots under each prospect's pre_draft_rankings (same ids) beside the four research mocks. runtime/draft.py reads the boards from this file and only the research_mocks from the evidence file, so each source counts once; a consumer averaging both files must do the same.
withdrawn_players_on_boards: Aaron Gray, Nick Fazekas, Richard Roby, Tiago Splitter appear on boards here but withdrew before the June 18, 2006 deadline (nba_2006_prospect_evidence.json, withdrawn_before_draft); they cannot be selected.
gaps: Yahoo! Sports, NBA.com, FOX Sports, Sporting News, HoopsWorld and USA Today 2006 mocks dated before the draft were not found in the Wayback Machine's index or behind bot challenges; ESPN Insider mocks (Chad Ford, June 12 and 19) are login-gated. SI.com's later mocks were not archived.
The InsideHoops mock was updated almost daily to the draft; the last archived version before the draft is June 14.
NBA.com's consensus board (draft2006/consensus.html) is archived only after the draft (2006-07-02), so its publication date cannot be verified and it was left out.
